The Vims gauntlet

Each piece of the voxel life sim is rebuilt round after round until a blind critic picks our render over the reference. Last updated Oct 07, 00:09 UTC.

Characters

Round 4 · reference won
Critic verdicts (4)
  1. R4RefCharacters are illegible at phone size because they are too small and lack face/silhouette contrast, worst on the beagle and the dad. The dog on the rug is a smeared orange/white blob with no readable head; per the reference it should be a ~1.5x larger chunky beagle lying in a clear side/3-4 pose: big brown floppy ears, white muzzle and blaze, black eye pixels and nose, tan saddle, tail up, chewing a blue bone. The dad stands with his face buried in a brown hair/beard mass against brown shelves; he should sit in the office chair at the desk with hands on keyboard (type pose), face turned 3/4 toward camera with lighter skin, clear eye pixels and a beard that is a distinct darker shape. The painter and the kid show the backs/tops of their hats; turn them 3/4 toward camera so eyes and smile read, sit painter on a stool at the easel with brush arm raised, kid cross-legged among toys. Scale all characters up ~25-35% (big chibi heads), and add a warm rim/key light or slight outline so they pop from same-hued furniture.
  2. R3RefCharacter posing/staging: Dad is rendered STANDING inside/behind the desk facing the camera with the office chair empty beside him, and the painter girl stands overlapping the easel. Per reference, Dad must be SEATED in the desk chair, back three-quarter to camera, hips at seat height, forearms forward on the keyboard (type anim); painter girl seated on a stool in front of the easel with brush arm raised to the canvas; music girl seated cross-legged on the rug. Also the beagle is an unreadable orange blob merged with a toy: it needs a clear lying-down silhouette (head on paws/bone, floppy dark-brown ears, white muzzle+chest, tan back, tail) separated from props, and faces need higher voxel density with distinct dark eyes and mouth so they read at phone size.
  3. R2RefCharacters are far too small and stiff to read on a phone: at the home_day camera each person is only ~60-80px tall and the dog ~50px, standing upright in idle poses. The reference gets about 2x the screen height per character (move the camera closer/lower FOV or scale the rigs up ~1.6x) and poses each one in its activity: dad SEATED on the office chair turned 3/4 toward the camera so his beard, eyes and hair read (ours shows only his back); bunny-hat girl SEATED on a stool facing the easel holding the brush up; bear-hat kid SITTING cross-legged on the rug holding a toy; beagle LYING stretched out (front paws forward, head on bone, tail up) next to the ball, not standing upright. Also give faces bigger eyes/mouth voxels and warm rim light so they pop against the furniture.
  4. R1RefCharacters' poses/facing and head proportions: the dad at the desk is rendered from directly behind (no visible face/beard, just a brown hair block on a plaid back) and the music kid is a stiff standing figure whose oversized lavender hat-head is ~60% of her height and hides her face. Per the reference: rotate/turn the dad to 3/4 profile, seated with arms forward typing, so beard+face read; shrink kids' heads to ~1:1.5 head:body chibi with hat sitting ON the head (ears on top, face fully exposed below brim), and pose the music kid sitting cross-legged on the rug playing with toys, the painter seated on a stool facing the easel with brush arm raised, and the beagle lying down chewing a bone with clear floppy ears, white muzzle and tan patches instead of the hunched sitting blob.

HUD

Round 4 · reference won
Critic verdicts (4)
  1. R4RefWorld-anchored action bubbles (Work/Paint/Practice) and skill chips are placed on top of the sims, covering their heads and faces. Work and Paint overlap the dad and the painter, Practice and +Music sit on the kid, and the plumbob is squeezed between Work and Paint. In the reference, each bubble floats clearly above its sim's head with a visible tail and about half a head of clear space. Chips are offset to the side and never cover a face, and the plumbob has its own space above the selected sim. Fix: anchor each bubble to the head bone plus a vertical offset in screen space (about 40-60px above the head top). Run a screen-space overlap pass that pushes bubbles and chips apart and away from the sims' screen bounds. Put the plumbob above the bubble or offset it so they don't collide. Make the bubble progress bars thicker (about 8px instead of about 5px).
  2. R3RefWorld-anchored action bubbles (Work/Paint/Play/Practice) are undersized and hard to read: scale each bubble up ~25% (about 170x60 at 1672w), icon ~32px, label ~18-20px Nunito ExtraBold, progress bar ~8px tall fully rounded with colour fill (blue Work, green Paint/Play, blue Practice) on light grey track, more inner padding, and a clear centred tail pointing down to the sim; skill chips (+ Creativity / + Music) likewise ~15% bigger. Secondary: need bars in the dark portrait panels should be thicker (~10px) with larger icons, matching the reference.
  3. R2RefWorld-anchored action bubbles float loose from their actors: the Work bubble and green plumbob hang ~100px above-left of the seated dad (over the monitor), and the Practice bubble plus '+ Music' chip hover far above the girl, so on a phone you can't tell which sim is doing what. Per the reference, anchor each bubble to the sim's head bone with a small fixed screen offset (~20-30px) so the tail tip touches just above the head, put the plumbob directly over the selected sim's head beside its bubble, stack skill chips just below/right of their bubble's tail, and shrink bubbles ~15% (smaller icon, tighter padding) so they don't dominate the scene.
  4. R1RefHousehold portrait cards (top-left): ours render the sim heads as small, soft, badly framed 3D captures - dad's face is cropped under hair, bunny-girl and cat-hat girl faces are tiny/washed out, dog is an unreadable smudge. Ref uses crisp, sharp, front-facing head-and-shoulders portraits filling ~85% of the white rounded card, face centred with clear eyes/smile, warm key light on a light backdrop. Fix the portrait camera (closer, eye-level, centred on face, no DOF/blur, higher render res). Secondary: action-bubble progress bars are stubby (~1/3 bubble width) and thin - make them span the full bubble width under the label, ~8px tall with rounded track like ref; add the missing season line under day/time in the clock panel.

House & lighting

Round 4 · reference won
Critic verdicts (4)
  1. R4RefCamera framing and scale: the home_night camera is too close/low and the props are oversized, so the house reads as a cropped jumble with no exterior. Pull the camera back and up (~1.6-2x distance, steeper ~45deg iso) so the whole two-storey cutaway house fits in frame with its dark wall caps and lower-floor facade/windows visible, and fill the void beyond with a lit neighbourhood (voxel houses with warm windows, rounded trees, street lamps along a road, moon). At that scale shrink the wall lanterns to small sconces with soft warm light pools (no blown white blocks), make characters ~1/3 room height and stage them readably (girl tucked in pink bunny bed with dad seated beside facing camera reading; kid at a proper bathroom vanity with mirror, sink and a glass shower stall, replacing the cupcake-like blob), and put the hallway/stair railing at the lower-right edge rather than centre-frame.
  2. R3RefFurniture and props are illegible voxel noise: the desk/monitors, cork board, piano, easel and dog are lumpy high-frequency blobs in near-identical orange-brown, unreadable at phone size. Rebuild key props as clean low-detail voxel models with crisp silhouettes and distinct material colours like the reference: a desk with 2 bright blue-screen monitors + laptop + mug + black office chair; a cork board with white/yellow pinned notes on the back wall; a black-and-white keyboard piano on a stand plus a tan guitar; an easel with a white canvas showing a pink bunny; a white-and-brown beagle with clear face. Also pull the camera back/lower so the tall back wall with large bright multi-pane windows (sunlight streaming in), framed pictures and the lower floor beyond the balcony railing are visible; reduce plant cube spam and the flat orange wash (keep warm light but add neutral walls/floor contrast) and limit tilt-shift to thin top/bottom bands.
  3. R2RefRoom interiors are under-furnished, flat empty boxes, and there is no warm practical lighting. In OUR shot the upstairs rooms are mostly bare pale wall and floor, with a few tiny props: a small pink bed, scattered toy blocks, a near-empty bathroom with a lone shower box. The walls are tall plain slabs, and only 2-3 weak light glows show up. The reference fills every room edge to edge at a larger furniture scale. The pink bunny bedroom has a full canopy-height bed with a plaid quilt, a bedside table and lamp, wall shelves of books and plushies, framed bunny pictures, plants and a rug. The star-blue bedroom has a blue star quilt bed, bookshelf, globe, telescope, desk and string lights. The bathroom has a glass shower with a towel, a wood vanity with sink, mirror and plants, and a bath mat. Wall sconces every ~2m cast strong amber light pools (OmniLights with warm colour, about 2x energy plus shadows) on walls and floor. Fix: scale furniture up ~1.3x, add 8-12 props per room along the walls (shelves, frames, plants, lamps), add lit sconces and lamps with real light falloff, and cut the cutaway walls down to a low wainscot height so they show the interiors instead of blank plaster. Secondary: the background is an unreadable blue blur. It needs visible neighbour houses with lit windows, street lamps, trees and a moon, with less aggressive tilt-shift so the ground floor stays readable.
  4. R1RefCamera/framing and depth: ours is shot too close and top-down with no visible lower floor, so the railing borders blur instead of revealing the downstairs room; pull the home_day camera back and lower its pitch (~35-40 deg) to frame the whole upstairs open-plan room plus, past the balcony railing in the lower-left, a populated lower floor (bookshelves, table lamps glowing, sofa) like the reference. Also fill the bare floor/walls: add cork board with pinned notes and framed landscape painting above the desk, dual monitors+printer+mug on desk, tall bookshelf with globe/trophy, guitar next to keyboard, toy box and soccer ball, hanging vines. And cut the global orange/yellow grade (reduce saturation/warm tint and exposure, restore contrast and neutral wood tones; window should not blow out).

Backyard BBQ

Round 4 · reference won
Critic verdicts (4)
  1. R4RefCharacters/guests at the dinner table: ours are tiny, low-detail blobs (~40px tall) hidden behind chairs and table, with no readable faces or hands, and deck guests read as stick figures. Per the reference, the diners need to be ~2x larger, with chunky voxel heads ~1/3 of body height, distinct faces (eyes, smiles, glasses), hair volume, arms raised holding drinks/burgers. They should be seated turned toward camera, with chair backs low enough not to hide them. Also move the camera closer/lower so the table group fills the centre third and the grill shows patties+corn+smoke.
  2. R3RefCharacters and table set-dressing: our guests are oversized blocky heads (head ~= torso width, crowding and occluding the table) so the scene reads as a pile of heads; the long checked table is nearly bare. Per reference: shrink heads to ~1/3 of body height with visible torsos/arms in seated poses on chairs around the table (back-of-head guests in foreground not blocking the tabletop), and load the table with plates of burgers, salad bowls, corn, drink glasses and a centre flower vase/candles along its full length; also the foreground dog is a blurry blob and the fire pit a plain grey box - give the dog a crisp patterned model in focus and the fire pit a stone ring with visible flames and the outdoor sofa fully framed.
  3. R2RefDusk lighting + empty lawn: the centre/foreground is a huge bright saturated green grass plane with uniform daylight-style lighting and nothing on it. Per ref, darken/desaturate the grass to dusk blue-green, make every lantern, string-light bulb and the fire pit cast warm orange OmniLight pools (bulbs should glow/bloom, not be flat white squares), light the house back with glowing sliding glass doors showing furnished interior under the pergola deck, and fill the empty lawn with lush voxel flower mounds (purple/pink/white/yellow), stepping-stone path and lanterns so the table group fills the frame; also reduce the foreground DOF blur smearing the bottom third.
  4. R1RefSKY + BACKDROP: ours has no visible sky at all - the top third is a blurred flat dark-purple house wall/haze with no horizon. Pull the camera/house back or lower the house so a purple-to-orange sunset gradient sky (orange/pink glow at horizon, violet above, a few clouds) is visible across the top 20-25% of frame, and add a row of dark silhouetted voxel neighbour houses with a few warm lit windows plus dark tree silhouettes along the horizon behind the fence. Also reduce the purple DOF/fog wash on the house so its lit sliding glass doors (showing warm furnished interior) and pergola with string lights on posts read crisply.

Autumn festival

Round 4 · reference won
Critic verdicts (4)
  1. R4RefPlaza composition/depth: stalls, stage, fountain, game booth and crowd are all crammed into one overlapping midground band with no open cobblestone floor. Fix per ref: clear a wide cobblestone walkway running from the bottom-center camera position back to the fountain (push FALL TREATS stall to the left edge, HANDMADE/game stalls to the right). Move the fountain into open view mid-depth, and set the stage further back as a raised platform with a dark roof/truss, so the guitarist reads against it instead of a flat red/white backdrop. Thin the crowd into spaced individuals along the path instead of stacked heads. Add many glowing warm string-light bulbs and emissive lamp-post lights. Shrink the oversized foreground lanterns/barrels so they frame the bottom edge instead of blocking it.
  2. R3RefCrowd and depth: our plaza has ~8 figures clumped at one mid-depth (mostly the oversized hero family overlapping each other) with large empty grey cobble between them; the ref fills the square with 20+ townsfolk at three distances (small figures by the fountain/stage, mid figures at stalls, big hero family in front), keeps heroes smaller (~1/4 screen height) and spaced apart so faces don't overlap, and adds foreground props (lanterns, flower barrels, chalkboard) instead of the blurred blocky tree mass. Also the stage guitarist is a dark unreadable blob - he needs to be lit, front-facing, with a visible guitar and music-note particles.
  3. R2RefFALL TREATS stall (front-left) is an empty box: the sign text is clipped by the awning ('TREATS' cut off) and the counter shows no food and no vendor. Per ref, it should be a wooden stall with a red/white striped awning ABOVE a fully visible carved sign with a maple-leaf icon, plus a vendor NPC behind a counter piled with candy apples, pies and pretzels in trays. Secondary: pull the camera back and down so a clear cobblestone path leads to the fountain and a larger, lit stage with the guitarist. Thin out the giant leaf-block clusters that bury the top third of the frame, and remove the dark foreground lantern silhouette at bottom-center.
  4. R1RefBackground/midground is lost in a blown-out yellow-orange haze: bloom+glow and depth-of-field blur are far too strong, so the town hall/clock tower, bunting, stage and crowd are unreadable smears and the whole frame has no value contrast. Cut bloom/glow intensity and DOF far-blur drastically (keep only mild blur past the fountain), lower exposure so cobbles are mid-grey-brown not beige-white, and then actually populate the backdrop per ref: a red-brick town hall with a crisp white clock face framed by large saturated orange/red voxel tree canopies on both sides, a raised wooden stage at back-right with a guitarist, maple-leaf banner and triangle bunting, string lights with discrete warm bulbs, black lamp posts with glowing lanterns, and a stone fountain centre-midground.

Grocery market

Round 4 · reference won
Critic verdicts (4)
  1. R4RefStore depth and shelf/produce density: our market is a shallow box where the back wall sits directly behind the signs, the grocery shelves are flat uniform stripes of colour, and the produce crates read as coloured strips. Per the reference: push the back wall far back and add 2-3 receding aisles of tall shelving lined with individual voxel packaged goods (cereal boxes, bottles, cans in varied sizes and colours, with gaps and facings), backlit fridge cases that emit a cool glow, and produce bins heaped above the rim with individually modelled tomatoes, carrots, banana bunches, apples and leafy greens, each fronted by a large readable $ price tag. Also add warm light pools under the pendant lamps, a few background shopper NPCs, and foreground props near the camera (checkout bananas, bottles, bags) so the frame feels full instead of showing empty floor.
  2. R3RefComposition/depth: camera is too close and the family (bunny girl, dad, dog, purple girl, cart, red basket) is piled into one overlapping clump in the centre, hiding the store. Per ref: pull camera back/raise it so a tiled aisle recedes to the back wall, spread the family out (dad pushing cart centre with dog riding in it, bunny girl at produce left, purple girl centre-right holding a cereal box) with clear floor gaps; then make the back of the store readable - fridge cases as tall glowing glass doors stocked with distinct milk cartons/bottles, and gondola shelves with recognisable box/can shapes instead of flat colour stripes.
  3. R2RefCamera + lighting: ours uses a high top-down camera that fills half the frame with flat, evenly-lit beige floor, and has no visible pendant lamps or warm light pools. The reference uses a low, eye-level camera (about 1.6 m high, pitched only ~10-15 degrees down, FOV ~55) looking down the aisle so the background shows wood ceiling beams with rows of hanging pendant lamps (black shade + emissive warm bulb + omni light, bloom/glow), brightly glowing back-lit fridge cases full of bottles, and the signs hanging large above. Its checkout counter sits in the near foreground with depth-of-field blur. Fix: lower and pull the market preset camera to eye level aimed down the main aisle, add 6-10 pendant lamps with warm OmniLights and glow, make fridge interiors emissive white/blue, and add contact shadows/SSAO so the floor is glossy tile with warm pools of light instead of a flat plane.
  4. R1RefCamera/composition: the market preset camera sits too low and close, so the family fills the middle third and hides the store; the fridge cases, shelves and back aisles shrink to a thin distant strip. Per the reference, pull the camera back and up (about 1.6-2x the distance, looking down roughly 25-30 deg) so the characters are about 1/3 of the frame height, make the produce wall on the left readable as distinct voxel tomatoes/carrots/bananas/apples in crates with $ tags, show a full row of lit fridge cases with bottles and tall shelves of distinct cereal-box packs in the midground, add 3-5 background shoppers, and cut the heavy DOF blur and orange haze for brighter, neutral-warm lighting.

Game loop

Round 2 · reference won
Critic verdicts (2)
  1. R2RefAutonomy breaks across floors. The playtest step autonomy_arrives FAILS: a starving Maya (hunger 0.05) autonomously picks Cook on the Fridge, then is still in phase=walk 50s later at 3x speed. She ends at y 3.00 -> 0.00 and never reaches the fridge or starts acting. That is exactly the Sims 3 moment of a hungry sim going downstairs to eat, and here it silently fails. Fix it in scripts/sim/sim_agent.gd (walk/stair-following and arrival logic) together with scripts/sim/nav_grid.gd (inter-level stair links and the final approach cell in front of interactables): add stuck detection with a repath, then a fallback to the next-best target, and make arrival tolerant so a multi-level autonomous path reliably ends in phase=act. Next biggest gap: social is just one-shot Chat/Hug actions. There are no relationship meters, no friend/romance progression, no social menu tiers and no non-household townies to meet, so the Sims 3 relationship loop is missing. Build a per-pair relationship value in scripts/core/game.gd, shown in a Relationships tab of the HUD panel (scripts/ui/hud.gd), with socials in scripts/sim/sim_actions.gd that unlock by relationship level. Catalogue depth (~15 items, no walls or floors in Build) is also far from Sims 3.
  2. R1RefNo mood layer and no consequences: needs just decay as bars (game.gd NEED_DECAY) and nothing reads them except autonomy scoring, so there are no moodlets, no overall mood, and no failure (no passing out at 0 energy, no bladder accident, no hunger warning, no refusing actions). Skills also jump in big chunks (Music 0->0.75 in one short session) with no skill panel, and the queued orders (sim_agent.gd MAX_QUEUE=3) have no visible queue strip to tap and cancel. Build it as follows. Add a mood/moodlet system in scripts/core/game.gd: per member, a moodlets list of {id, icon, label, delta, expires}, an overall mood computed from needs plus moodlets, and a mood_changed signal. In sim_agent.gd, low needs push negative moodlets (Hungry, Tired, Bored, Smelly, Lonely), and completing actions, skill level-ups and tasks push positive ones (Well Rested, Had Fun, Learned Something). Mood scales skill gain and work pay, and need=0 forces an action (pass out / accident) that adds a strong negative moodlet. In scripts/ui/, add a mood plumbob colour (green/yellow/red) on plumbob.gd and portrait.gd, a moodlet row in need_panel.gd, a Sims-3-style action-queue strip of icons next to the selected portrait (tap to cancel), and a skills tab showing level 1-10 bars.
